Subject: Intermittent request delays observed - sample logs attached

Hi Lauren,

We're seeing a handful of requests to your /v1/infer endpoint that returned much higher p95 latency (~3.8s) than usual (~400ms) between 13:43-13:57 PST today. No full failures, just slower responses that affected a small portion of our users. I attached a short log slice and one request-id for reference.

Can the Redwood team confirm whether there were any platform-side slowdowns or retries in that window? We did a quick check on our side and didn't find retries or heavy bursts.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
SRE Lead, SunGrid AI

- If you can share a short sample prompt/size (token counts), that helps replicate.

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, Sam Patel <sam.patel@sungrid.ai>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:18:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent request delays observed - sample logs attached

Hi Sam, Lauren — I reviewed the trace we have for the request-id. Internal findings:
- No platform-wide incident recorded in the US-west region for 2026-11-02 13:40-14:00 PST.
- The particular request shows the serving pod handled the call in ~420ms at the runtime level.
- We see a downstream client-side retry in your logs that caused an extra re-issue within the same second. That pattern can surface as higher apparent p95 on aggregate if retries are included in your measurement window.

Could you confirm whether your instrumentation deduplicates retries before computing p95? If not, we recommend ignoring retried attempts when calculating latency percentiles.

I attached an anonymized Redwood trace export to illustrate the timing.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@sungrid.ai>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:04:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent request delays observed - sample logs attached

Thanks Marcus — that trace is helpful. I checked our side and confirmed we did not intentionally trigger a retry, but our client SDK had an automatic short-circuit retry for connection blips enabled in that version. It looks like two brief connection attempts happened (13:44:10.322 and 13:44:10.397); both returned 200 but recorded separately in our telemetry.

We'll flip the dedupe and retry behavior in a staging branch and validate. Appreciate the quick analysis.

One request: can Redwood confirm there were no queued tasks or GC pauses on the serving host at that time? We want to be confident this was purely client-side.

Sam

---

From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@sungrid.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent request delays observed - sample logs attached

Hi Sam — quick follow-up from runtime telemetry and host metrics:
- We examined GC/host CPU and IO for the serving hosts that served that request-id. No GC spikes, no CPU saturation, and no disk IO contention were observed in the 5-minute window around 13:44 PST.
- No autoscale or routing events were active for your dedicated pool in that minute.
- The trace Marcus shared shows the two client attempts were served independently and completed quickly on our side (~410-430ms).

Conclusion: we do not see evidence of a platform-induced latency spike. The behavior aligns with split client attempts being measured separately on your side.

Recommended next steps:
1) Update your client SDK to deduplicate retries before computing latency metrics (or filter by request-id).
2) If you still see elevated p95 after dedupe, collect full request+response traces for a sample of affected requests and re-open the support ticket (SG-8241) with those attachments.

I'll mark this thread as closed from our side, but please re-open if anything contradicts the above. Thanks for the thorough logs and patience.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
